description:
We are Brochachos, a five-member student team from Baku, Azerbaijan, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our goal is to create an interactive lunar mission training experience that helps students understand space exploration and engineering decisions using NASA resources.

We are passionate about technology, software development, space science, and education. We aim to combine creativity, teamwork, and AI-assisted development to build an impactful project.
summary:
OUTPOST REPLAY is a free, browser-based mission trainer for ages 7–12, in English and Azerbaijani. Players lead a two-person crew through nine simulated days at a fictional outpost near the Moon's Shackleton Crater, making six decisions that trade off power, life support, radiation exposure and science.

It addresses the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge through one learning loop: Predict, Decide, Observe, Rewind, Compare, Learn. After a run, players rewind a single decision, keep everything else fixed, and see exactly what changed and why, as in a controlled experiment.

The scenarios draw on NASA resources, including DONKI space-weather records and the OSDR VEG-01A plant study, with every classroom assumption clearly labeled. This matters because it teaches children systems thinking and evidence-based reasoning, not just space facts
details:
OUTPOST REPLAY is a browser game where players aged 7–12 lead a two-person crew through nine simulated days (216 hours) at a fictional outpost near the Moon's Shackleton Crater.

How it works: The player makes six decisions about solar power, habitat setup, a 72-hour shadow, ice prospecting, a solar storm and mission close-out. A deterministic simulation tracks battery energy, oxygen, water, food, radiation dose and science points hour by hour. After a run, Rewind & Compare lets the player change one decision, keep all other inputs fixed, and see the exact differences with a short engineering explanation. A bonus mission moves the same ideas to a Mars dust storm with a 14-minute radio delay.

Benefits and intended impact: Children practice prediction, controlled experiments and trade-off thinking. Cadet Mode uses plain story language; Engineer Mode shows full units for teachers. The game runs in English and Azerbaijani.

Creativity: Instead of restarting after failure, players rewind one choice and compare two runs side by side.

Factors considered: Accessibility (two languages, keyboard controls, two reading levels), cost (free, open source, no install or account), and scientific honesty (measured data, published models and classroom assumptions are labeled separately). No classroom learning study has been completed yet.

Tools: TypeScript, React, Vite, Phaser, Three.js, Recharts, Tailwind CSS. Source code: https://github.com/Newgenzzz/outpost-replay-team
